chunks: As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā, from al-ʿĪṣ ibn al-Qāsim, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, that he said:

Regarding a man who performed ʿumrah in Rajab, he said: if he remains in Makkah until he departs from it as a pilgrim, then the hady has become obligatory upon him. But if he leaves Makkah so that he enters ihram from somewhere other than it, then there is no hady upon him.

So the proper way to understand this report is one of two things: either it is to be understood as referring to merit and recommendation rather than obligation and requirement; or it is to be understood as referring to one who performed ʿumrah in Rajab and remained in Makkah until the months of hajj, then performed tamattuʿ from it by ʿumrah toward hajj. For whoever is like that, the hady is binding upon him according to what this report contains, and that indicates it.

key_terms.الِاسْتِحْبَابِ: recommended status rather than strict obligation
key_terms.الْهَدْيُ: the sacrificial offering required in certain hajj circumstances
key_terms.تَمَتَّعَ: performed tamattuʿ, combining ʿumrah with hajj in the prescribed manner
key_terms.رَجَبٍ: the month of Rajab, in which the ʿumrah was performed
key_terms.مَكَّةَ: Makkah, where the pilgrim remains or departs from

ai.seo_question: Does hady become obligatory for someone who performs ʿumrah in Rajab and then goes on to hajj?
ai.summary: This report discusses the ruling of hady for a person who performs ʿumrah in Rajab and later proceeds to hajj. It explains that the report may either indicate recommendation rather than obligation, or apply specifically to one who remains in Makkah until the hajj season and performs tamattuʿ, in which case the hady becomes binding.
